title: List project members for reviewer routing
description: Return the people who can review work on this project — one row per member with access to it, each with their `user_uuid`, `email`, `first_name`/`last_name`, resolved GitHub `login` (null when they have no linked GitHub identity), and the `teams` they belong to. The cold-start reviewer-routing path: when a finding's owner can't be read off a fetched entity's `created_by` and there's no cached `reviewer:<area>` memory or inbox precedent, list members, match the owner by email/name, then put their `user_uuid` in `suggested_reviewers` on `scout-emit-report` / `scout-edit-report`. Every member is routable this way; a null `github_login` only means no draft PR can be opened as that person. Pass `search` to narrow a large roster by name or email. Pass `team` with a bare team slug (no `@org/` prefix) to turn a slug from a note, from CODEOWNERS, or from an owners file into the people on that team, maintainers first: take the first 1 to 3 rows, which is the cap `suggested_reviewers` enforces anyway. A `team` that resolves to nobody comes back as an error saying which case it hit, because team rosters sync one by one and a slug with no rows almost always means it isn't synced here rather than that the team doesn't exist. The roster is a periodic snapshot, so it can lag the live team. Strictly team-scoped.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription: Case-insensitive substring filter over member email and first/last name. Use it to narrow a large project's roster to the owner you're trying to match instead of pulling every member.

layers.text: Case-insensitive substring filter over member email and first/last name. Use it to narrow a large project's roster to the owner you're trying to match instead of pulling every member.

typeDocumentation.effectiveDescription: Team slug (case-insensitive, no `@org/` prefix), for example `team-desktop`. Narrows the roster to the members on that team, maintainers first, so a slug from a scout note, CODEOWNERS, or an owners file resolves to people you can route to. Returns an error, not an empty list, when the project has no synced team roster or the roster holds no rows for the slug.
